title: Evaluating Antibacterial Effect of Moth-Eye Films
author: Kiyoshi Minoura
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ipkcdkw
materials: PET film was used as a control film.
All sample films were disinfected with ethanol.

steps.title: Prepare Bacterial Cultures
steps.instruction: Culture S. aureus (NBRC12732) and E. coli (NBRC3972) to prepare the microbial solution.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate one colony on a new NA plate (Nissui Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd.) and culture overnight at 37℃.
Perform a second culture and suspend the bacteria in 1/500 nutrient broth (1/500 NB; Eiken Chemical Co. Ltd.) at McFarland Standard 1.0 (approximately 10^8 cfu/ml).

steps.title: Dilute Bacterial Suspension
steps.instruction: Adjust the bacterial density for the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the S. aureus or E. coli suspension 100 times with 1/500 NB to reach a final bacterial density between 2.5×10^6 and 10×10^6 cfu/ml.

steps.title: Fabricate Moth-Eye Films (Sample A)
steps.instruction: Create nano-structured films using an anodized and etched aluminum moth-eye stamper (pitch and height ~200nm).

substeps.instruction: Spread urethane trifunctional acrylate resin with polyethylene glycol (PEG) spacers on a base substrate film (75 μm poly ethylene terephthalate thickness).
Laminate the substrate film with the resin using a nip roll on the moth-eye stamper.
Expose the resin to ultraviolet light.
Peel the cured film off the stamper by hand to obtain Sample A.

steps.title: Fabricate Flat Surface Films (Sample B)
steps.instruction: Create control flat films using the same process as Sample A, but substitute the moth-eye stamper with a flat glass stamper.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Films
steps.instruction: Cut all sample films into 5cm squares.

steps.title: Inoculate Sample Films
steps.instruction: Apply the microbial solution to the films.

substeps.instruction: Place the sample film in the center of a petri dish.
Drop 10 μl of the final microbial solution onto the sample film.
Keep in a safety cabinet at room temperature for the indicated time.

steps.title: Recover Bacteria from Films
steps.instruction: Wash the bacteria off the film surface using SCDLP medium.

substeps.instruction: Pour 9.6 ml of fresh soybean-casein digest broth with lecithin and polysorbate 80 (SCDLP; Wako Pure Chemical Industries Ltd.) directly onto the sample film in the petri dish.
Wash out attached bacteria by shaking the petri dish for 30 sec at 500 rpm/min using a vortex mixer.
Repeat the wash process three times using the SCDLP medium collected from the petri dish.
Collect all SCDLP medium (approximately 10ml) into a 50mL conical centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Quantify Bacterial Colonies
steps.instruction: Plate and culture the recovered bacteria to count colonies.

substeps.instruction: Serially 10-fold dilute the bacterial suspension with PBS.
Quickly mix 1 ml of each diluted sample with 9 ml of melted Pearl Core plate count agar (PC; Eiken Chemical Co. Ltd.) kept at 50℃ in a water bath.
Pour the mixture onto a petri dish and cool to room temperature.
Culture the bacteria in Pearl Core plate count agar for 24 hours at 37℃.
Count the number of visible colonies in the dish.
